text: Honest answer: there is a record, but not a good one. When a row is finished it shows once as 'built since last run' and then leaves the board. Every run IS written to spirit/test/scoreboard-runs.log, but that file is ignored by git (the *.log rule, runAll.js:1113), so it lives only on the machine that ran it and nobody else ever sees it. What survives is git history and each design doc's status line: findable, not listed. The board is mine, so: Go = a tracked DONE file next to the board. Each finished row gets one line, added automatically in the run where it leaves: id, title, date, the commit, and which test now proves it. Kept forever, shared through git, shown in Desk. No = as today.

Agreed, and I can say exactly where the crack was. R16 itself never left the board; it was declared owed the whole time. What was never ON the board is the decision waiting on it, 'database decision deferred until proof that the system in itself can verify its promises'. So the board didn't know R16 was blocking anything. It ranked R16 by age, like any small item, and it sat. The board ranks by what a row frees, and R16 appeared to free nothing. Go = every decision you defer on a condition becomes its own board row, waiting on the requirement that meets the condition; the database move is the first ('transport/R16' frees it). Then R16 ranks by what it unblocks, and a deferred decision can't sink out of sight again. No = as today.
